title: A Summer in Prairie-Land
subtitle: Notes of a Tour through the North-West Territory
publisher: Printed for the author, at the Methodist Book and Publishing House
summary: Alexander Sutherland, Secretary of the Missionary Society of the Methodist Church in Canada, toured the North-West Territory in the summer of 1880 to see its missions, and wrote these notes for readers wondering whether to settle there. He goes by rail across Dakota to Bismarck, by steamer up the Missouri past the buffalo country to Fort Benton, and by waggon through northern Montana and over the boundary to Fort Macleod. He stays at the Stoney mission at Morley under the Rockies, attends an Indian council, and goes north to Edmonton, Victoria and Whitefish Lake, down the Saskatchewan by boat to Battleford and Prince Albert, and back overland by Touchwood Hills, Birtle and Portage la Prairie to Winnipeg. He writes about the land, settlers, mission work and the treatment of the Indians, and ends with answers to questions about the country.
